title: RequirementSpec
description: The typed interpretation of a user's brief. Produced by the Interpret stage, confirmed before generation, and consumed by every later stage. Every requirement names the checker that decides it, so no requirement can be asserted without evidence.

brief.description: Verbatim record of what the user asked for.

lane.description: Which composition path the spec selects. symbolic_first when mechanical requirements dominate, audio_first when the brief is mostly aesthetic.

oracle.description: Which compliance oracle is permitted for this spec. 'none' means deterministic gates only, and every semantic requirement is reported unverified.

assumptions.description: Inferred or defaulted requirements still awaiting confirmation. Generation must not start while this is non-empty in interactive mode.

id.description: Stable identifier used to key answers, map repairs, and report verdicts.

text.description: The requirement as a person would state it, for display in the compliance report.

kind.description: mechanical = exactly computable in code; semantic = a judgment; policy = a safety or rights constraint with its own action thresholds.

verify.description: Names the checker, not a description. A requirement whose only checker is human.* cannot be enforced automatically and is reported as such.

severity.description: hard = a failure rejects the candidate; soft = contributes to the composite score; policy = uses the policy action thresholds.

source.description: Provenance. Inferred requirements must be confirmed; defaults are never silently promoted to explicit.

confirmed.description: True once the user has confirmed an inferred requirement.

target.description: The requirement's value in the shape the named checker expects. Numeric targets are always compared in code.

stage_enforced.description: The earliest stage at which this requirement becomes observable. Requirements are enforced here, not later.

repair_hint.description: Instruction template used by the repair router when this requirement fails. Code fills it; the oracle never writes it.
